title: Send data from a collector you already run

blocks.content: You already run a collector — Prometheus, for example — and it stays. You'll point it at Grafana Cloud so what it collects is stored there too. Nothing new gets installed. This guide walks one method: Prometheus remote write, Prometheus's built-in way to forward metrics.
First, open the setup page for hosted Prometheus metrics:
Click **Connections** in the main menu.
Click **Add new connection**.
Search for **Hosted Prometheus** to filter the catalog.
Click the **Hosted Prometheus metrics** tile.
The setup page is open. Everything you need — the destination address, a credential, and the configuration — comes from here.
Now create a token and copy the configuration. You need the **Admin** role in your stack:

blocks.title: Create a token and copy the config

blocks.content: Choose to forward metrics with your existing **Prometheus** server, not Grafana Alloy. The page adjusts its instructions to match.

Create a new API token: give it a name you'll recognize and click **Create token**. The token is how Prometheus signs in to your stack, and the page adds it to the configuration snippet for you. Type nothing by hand.
Copy the configuration snippet. It's a `remote_write` block: the endpoint to send to, your stack's username, and the token as the password.
You have what this page exists to give you: a `remote_write` block with your stack's address and credentials.
Next, add it to Prometheus on the machine that runs it:

On the machine running Prometheus, open `prometheus.yml` and paste the snippet at the end of the file. If the file already has a `remote_write` section, add the new endpoint under the existing one instead.
Restart Prometheus to load the change — `systemctl restart prometheus` on most Linux hosts. Your scrape configs, recording rules, and alerts don't change. Prometheus just gains a second destination.
Prometheus is forwarding every metric it scrapes to Grafana Cloud.
Finally, confirm the data is arriving:
Click **Explore** in the main menu.
Open the picker and choose the data source whose name ends in **-prom**. Every stack comes with one — it reads the metrics you just sent.
blocks.tooltip: Every query runs against one of your connected data stores. This picker chooses which one.

blocks.content: In the query field, enter `up` — the simplest Prometheus query: one row per target your Prometheus scrapes.
Click **Run query**. Rows coming back means your metrics are in Grafana Cloud. If it's empty, give it a minute after the restart and run it again.
Your collector didn't change — it just sends to Grafana Cloud now, and you queried the result.

One habit worth starting now: what you send is what usage-based billing counts. Prometheus can filter what remote write forwards — `write_relabel_configs` in the same block — so send the metrics you use, not everything you scrape.
